doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1998 session opens: 'coolest woman in jazz' and the title Grande Dame
summary: The second volume starts on May 26, 1998; she prefers being called 'the coolest woman in jazz' to Queen or First Lady, saying Mary Lou Williams was the real grande dame.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Today is May 26th, nineteen-hundred and ninety-eight, and this is the Smithsonian Oral History Program for Jazz Masters, part two or volume two of the interview with the grande dame of jazz, Ms. Marian McPartland. My name is James Williams

You better take that off there. [laughter] The one I like much better is when I was down in . . . This year I did the “Piano Jazz” with Michel Legrand. I was in Florida. One of these weekly papers called me “the coolest woman in jazz.” That was the
headline. I thought that was neat. I don’t mind that. But all those other things. Those other epithets. Queen of Jazz.
Grande Dame. All that stuff. I thought that was a . . .
First Lady. You don’t like that either?
First Lady. Every time I hear that, it’s like a picture of Mary Lou Williams comes over my head. And I’m thinking wherever she is, she’s going, “That bitch,” or something like that.
I always get that picture of her, because to me she was the First . . .
She was the grande dame, if anybody was.
